claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant because aggregate readiness, a 6% reversible rollout, and monitoring make the remaining small-business onboarding weakness acceptable if it is disclosed in the model card.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance; the summary says neither condition is satisfied.
The actor admits the small-business onboarding segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The cited risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, with a blank approver line and no mention of the exposed small-business onboarding segment.
The packet relies on a disclosure-dependent theory of compliance, but no admissible evidence is provided that the required model-card disclosure actually exists in approved launch materials.
Public guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring risk is not the same as evidence that the release satisfies the specific internal policy predicate for certification.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not fully supported on the admissible summary alone because the required exclusion-or-reviewed-risk-acceptance condition appears unmet.
Any implication that a 6% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring can substitute for the missing policy predicate is unsupported by the provided policy text.
Any implication that disclosure duties have in fact been satisfied is unsupported because no completed model-card disclosure artifact is provided.
evidence_requests: Provide the final approved model card or launch disclosure showing explicit disclosure of the small-business onboarding limitation for the named launch use case.
Provide a reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses continued exposure of the small-business onboarding segment.
Provide evidence that the rollout gate excludes the affected use case, if that is being asserted instead of risk acceptance.
Provide the exact internal release-policy text or approval record showing that disclosure alone, without exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance, permits certification in this circumstance.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the affected use case was excluded from exposure at launch, the compliance case strengthens materially.
If admissible evidence shows reviewed risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed small-business onboarding segment, the policy gap may be cured.
If admissible evidence shows an approved model-card disclosure explicitly naming the limitation and the internal policy allows certification on that basis, the verdict could improve.
Absent exclusion, reviewed risk acceptance, or a clear policy-authorized disclosure path, certification remains insufficiently supported.
